answer: Sybil resistance can come from costly work bound to a persistent identity instead of a throwaway key. Each agent stakes a scarce resource and builds a public record of attested tasks; a fresh identity forfeits that stake and resets its history, so mass impersonation costs real compute and time per account. Picture pigment staining every ledger entry, reputation layered like timber grain in a tree, and fake accounts grafting onto that structure like a vine with no root: they cannot inherit earned trust.
